Prevention: Yam mosaic virus can be spread through infected planting material and by aphid vectors.
Use seed yams produced from healthy plants - this can be obtained through tagging of healthy plants
Avoid using small under-sized tubers for planting materials as these are likely to be infected by the virus
Collect all old plant debris and volunteer crops from field and destroy by burning
Effective control of weeds that are possible alternate hosts for aphid vectors
Avoid intercropping with susceptible yam species
Avoid injuries to plants when working in the field as
YMV can also be transmitted mechanically
Monitoring: Monitor plants weekly looking at the surfaces of leaves for the presence of aphids.
The aphids are small (1-1.5 mm) soft bodied insects often yellow to very dark (almost black) green in colour
Monitor young leaves as growth progresses for mosaic appearance, chlorosis, leaf distortions and stunted growth.
Infection can occur at all stages of development
Farmers should start action at first sign of disease to avoid being overwhelmed by spread and severity
Direct Control: Rogue out infected plants showing symptoms at early stages of growth and destroy by burning
Farmers generally will not rogue their yam plants so this activity should be limited to early stages of growth
There are no chemicals to control this viral disease but insecticides can help to control the insect vector
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
Application of chemical control may not be practiced by small scale farmers for economic reasons
Spray field and surrounding areas with imidacloprid at 5-7ml/15L of water to control aphids if vector population persists.
A systemic neonicotinoid insecticide, IRAC group: 4A
Apply two times at intervals of 7-14 days
Spray alpha-cypermethrin at 5-7.5ml/15L of water to control the aphids.
A contact and ingested pyrethroid insecticide, IRAC group: 3A
Apply two times at 7-14 days interval depending on vector situation.
Alternate with other chemical group insecticide after two applications.
